label: <DEL> delimiter step, strongest in long sequences
explanation: Low end of candidate unit 18 fires mainly on the <DEL> delimiter step (recall_idx 0). That step holds 81% of activation mass and the unit fires on 43% of delimiter steps. Firing rate and magnitude grow with sequence length: rate rises from about 3% at L<=5 to about 7% at L=9, and to_go=8 gives a 40% rate. Magnitude is also raised when the first original token (the token about to be output) is one of w, d, 0, z, c, f; all top activations are <DEL> steps in sequences that start with these tokens. The remaining 19% of mass is weaker firing on copy-phase steps, mostly the first copy step (recall_idx 1, 12.5% of mass), plus a small tail on late copy steps. It essentially never fires during the original-token phase (28 of 646k steps). Restricting to delimiter steps with L>=7 trades recall for precision; plain phase==1 has mass recall 0.81 but precision 0.43, because many short-sequence delimiters do not fire.
